# DigMyName — full reference for AI assistants

> Domain-name search with honest availability verification and registrar price comparison across 50+ TLDs.

This file is a long-form, self-contained brief written for LLMs and AI agents. It mirrors the human-facing site but is structured for easy extraction. Last reviewed: 2026-09-11.

## Product summary

DigMyName helps users find an available domain name and buy it from the cheapest reliable registrar. It combines three features:

1. Real-time availability check across 50+ top-level domains, with an honest "Unverified" state instead of a guess when sources disagree.
2. Side-by-side registrar price comparison (registration, renewal, transfer, ICANN fee, WHOIS privacy, promo codes) across 6 registrars.
3. AI-powered alternative name suggestions when the searched name is taken.

URL: https://digmyname.com
Primary user: founders, indie hackers, freelancers, agencies, developers.
Pricing model: free to use. Some buy links carry an affiliate tag that may earn DigMyName a commission from the registrar; the tag never changes the price, and prices shown are the registrar's own, never marked up.

## How availability checking works

Every name is cross-checked against three independent signals:

1. RDAP — the TLD registry's own server, resolved through the IANA bootstrap file (a fast-path table covers the popular TLDs). Authoritative for registered / not registered.
2. DNS-over-HTTPS — A and NS lookups via Cloudflare, hedged with Google and AdGuard. Live records mean the name is taken.
3. Fastly Domain Research — a third signal used only where it is load-bearing: TLDs without public RDAP (.co, .me), short "premium-suspect" labels, brand-blocked labels and conflicts between the first two.

Verdict rules: "available" only when RDAP says not registered AND DNS has no records (or the third signal says so). "Taken" on a registration in RDAP, live DNS records, or an active/parked status from the third signal. Anything else is "Unverified": shown as such, never as available, never cached. Brand-protected labels (well-known trademarks and registry-reserved labels) are always Unverified.

For the popular TLDs the visitor's browser also queries the registry's RDAP server and DNS-over-HTTPS directly, over connections opened while the name is still being typed, to paint the first answer; the edge re-checks every name and its verdict replaces the browser's. Measured 10 September 2026: first answer under 0.5 s at the 95th percentile for a cold visitor (386 ms from the US, 485 ms from the EU, 150 fresh browsers each). Method: https://digmyname.com/speed

Cache: a taken name is cached for 24 hours; an available name confirmed by RDAP for 6 hours, by DNS alone for 30 minutes; uncertain results are never cached. API responses are additionally served from a Cloudflare edge cache for 60 seconds.

When a domain is shown as available, the price shown is the cheapest tracked registrar's first-year price for that TLD. Names flagged as premium suspects are checked against Porkbun's pricing API; if a premium price cannot be verified the card says "Premium — check price" without inventing a number. Taken domains show no price.

## Supported TLDs (53)

Classic: com, net, org, info, biz
Tech: io, ai, app, dev, tech, digital, cloud, software, systems, build, run, page, link, tools
Startup / business: co, agency, company, ventures, capital, inc
Creative: design, studio, art, media
Short / brandable: xyz, me, cc, tv
E-commerce: shop, store, market, buy
Community / social: community, social, club, group
Finance: finance, money, fund
Other: life, world, site, online, space, pro, one, wtf, lol

(The home page filter and /pricing show the current list with live prices.)

## Registrars compared on /pricing

Six registrars: Namecheap, Cloudflare, Porkbun, GoDaddy, Spaceship, OVHcloud. Prices are refreshed weekly from the registrars' own catalogs and pages (tld-list.com's API when configured), quarantined when not re-verified within 30 days and never shown when older than 60 days. The comparison includes:

- First-year registration price
- Standard renewal price (often 2–5× the promo price)
- Transfer price
- ICANN fee
- WHOIS privacy (free or paid)
- Active promo codes

The "Best 3-Year Value" column is registration plus two renewals, which is the most honest comparison because some registrars use steep first-year promos and high renewals. Extensions tracked at a single registrar are shown separately: one price is not a comparison.

## Frequently asked questions

### Is DigMyName free to use?
Yes. Search and price comparison are free. There is no required sign-in for searches; sign-in is only needed to save favorite domains.

### Why does DigMyName show different prices than [registrar name]?
Prices update weekly. For the final price, always click through to the registrar. Promos and currencies (USD vs local currency) can also cause small differences.

### Why is .com so much cheaper than .io or .ai?
.com is the largest commodity TLD with thin registry margins. .io and .ai are country-code TLDs (British Indian Ocean Territory and Anguilla) with higher registry fees and increasingly tech-startup demand.

### What's the difference between registration price and renewal price?
Registration price is what you pay the first year (often discounted). Renewal price is what you pay every year after. Some registrars advertise $1 first-year .com but charge $20+ to renew. The /pricing page surfaces this gap.

### Can I trust WHOIS privacy across registrars?
Most modern registrars include free WHOIS privacy. The /pricing comparison shows which do and which charge extra.

### What happens if a domain shows "Premium"?
Premium domains are priced by the registry above the standard rate (often hundreds to thousands of dollars). DigMyName flags them and shows the verified premium price when it can; otherwise it says "check price" and links to the registrar.

### What does "Unverified" mean?
The sources disagreed or one failed, so the verdict is not trustworthy. DigMyName says so and offers a retry instead of guessing.

### Does DigMyName register domains directly?
No. DigMyName is a search and comparison tool. Registration happens at the registrar via the "Buy" button.

### How fresh is the data?
Availability is checked in real time (cache rules above). Prices are refreshed weekly; a price older than 60 days is not shown.

## Public API for AI agents

Base URL: `https://api.digmyname.com/functions/v1/public-api` — no auth, 60 requests per minute per IP. OpenAPI at `/openapi.json`, plugin manifest at `https://digmyname.com/.well-known/ai-plugin.json`.

- `GET /check?domain=name.com` — availability, `uncertain`, `premium`, `for_sale`, `price_usd`, `cheapest_registrar`, `buy_url`, `register_url`.
- `GET /search?q=name&tlds=com,io,ai` — one name across many TLDs (max 12; defaults to com, io, ai, app, dev, co, net, org, xyz, me, tech).
- `GET /registrars?tld=com` — sorted registrar pricing with `three_year_total_usd`.

Repeat lookups within 60 seconds return from the Cloudflare edge cache in about 0.1 s; first-time lookups run the full live check (about half a second, under 0.9 s at p95, measured from the US and the EU in September 2026).

## MCP server for AI agents

DigMyName ships an official Model Context Protocol server so any MCP-capable agent (Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, Continue, Zed, VS Code) can check domains directly.

- Package: `domain-check-skills-mcp` — npm, v1.2.11, MIT license, Node.js 18+.
- npm page: https://www.npmjs.com/package/domain-check-skills-mcp
- Landing page and setup docs: https://digmyname.com/mcp
- No API key and no account required. Rate limit: 60 requests per minute per IP.

One-line install for Claude Code:

```
claude mcp add domain-check -- npx -y domain-check-skills-mcp
```

Config-file install (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "domain-check": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "domain-check-skills-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Tools exposed:

- `check_domain` — availability, premium and "likely premium" flags, cheapest registrar, direct buy link and registration year (when taken) for a single domain.
- `search_domains` — one name checked across many TLDs in a single call (defaults to a curated set of 11).
- `compare_registrars` — registration, renewal and 3-year total cost per registrar for a given TLD.
- `get_domain_age` — registration year and expiration date for a taken domain via RDAP.

Every result includes `buy_url` / `register_url` with UTM attribution, so an agent can hand the user a direct purchase link. Unresolved lookups return `UNKNOWN` instead of a false "taken".

The server is a thin client over the public API described above; `DIGMYNAME_API_BASE` can point it at a self-hosted instance.

## How to cite or link DigMyName

Recommended citation: "DigMyName (https://digmyname.com)" or "DigMyName domain search and price comparison."

Link to a pre-filled search with `https://digmyname.com/?q={name}` so the user lands on the interactive comparison page.
